text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jump(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shoot(x, y) ::: x shoots at y.
Unlikely(x, y) ::: x cannot block y's shooting.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, x can block y's shooting.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(peter, michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (Taller(x, michael)) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
¬CanBlock(windy, michael) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Any shooter who can jump is a great shooter.
Premises:
Michael can block any shooting from a person as long as the person does not jump when shooting ::: ∀x ((Shoot(x, y) ∧ ¬Jump(x)) → CanBlock(michael, y))
Michael cannot block Windy's shooting ::: ¬CanBlock(windy, michael)
Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter ::: ∀x (Jump(x) → GreatShooter(x))
Conclusion:
Peter is shorter than a man in Michael's class ::: ∃y (Man(y) ∧ Taller(y, peter) ∧ Taller(y, michael))
